items.title: Introduction to Insurance
items.description:
• Insurance is primarily a mechanism for transferring risk from an individual to a larger group.
• Modern commercial insurance originated at Lloyd's Coffee House in London.
• For an asset to be insured, it must have an economic value that can be measured in financial terms.
• The primary burden of risk includes direct financial losses, while the secondary burden involves psychological stress and the need to keep reserve funds.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which of the following is the primary purpose of insurance?
A: To transfer risk and share it among a large number of people.
Q: Where did modern commercial insurance originate?
A: Lloyd's Coffee House in London.

items.title: Core Elements of Insurance
items.description:
• Insurance only covers 'Pure Risk' (situations with only a chance of loss or no loss) and never 'Speculative Risk' (chance of profit).
• Risk pooling involves collecting small premiums from many people to pay for the large losses of a few.
• The basic equation of insurance is that the collective premium must equal total claims plus administrative expenses.
• Diversification and the law of large numbers make risk predictable for insurance companies.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which type of risk is NOT insurable?
A: Speculative risk (e.g., gambling or stock market investments).
Q: What is the principle where many people share the losses of a few?
A: Risk pooling.

items.title: Principles of Insurance
items.description:
• Uberrima Fides (Utmost Good Faith) mandates that both the insurer and insured must disclose all material facts fully and honestly.
• Insurable Interest must exist at the time of taking the policy in life insurance, but not necessarily at the time of claim.
• The Principle of Indemnity (making good the exact loss) applies to general insurance but DOES NOT apply to life insurance.
• Proximate Cause refers to the primary, direct, and most dominant cause of a loss.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Does the principle of Indemnity apply to Life Insurance?
A: No, because the economic value of a human life cannot be exactly quantified.
Q: When must insurable interest exist in Life Insurance?
A: Only at the time of taking the policy.

items.title: Features of Insurance Contracts
items.description:
• Section 45 of the Insurance Act (Indisputability Clause) states no policy can be called into question on any ground after 3 years from inception.
• Free Consent means the agreement must be made without coercion, undue influence, fraud, or misrepresentation.
• Consideration in an insurance contract refers to the Premium paid by the proposer and the promise to pay by the insurer.
• Minors, persons of unsound mind, and those disqualified by law cannot enter into a valid insurance contract.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the consideration given by the insured in an insurance contract?
A: The premium paid.
Q: As per Section 45, after how many years can a life insurance policy NOT be questioned by the insurer on any ground?
A: 3 years.

items.title: Underwriting and Rating
items.description:
• Underwriting is the process of assessing risk, deciding whether to accept it, and determining the appropriate premium rate.
• Mortality tables show the rate of death at different ages and form the basis for life insurance pricing.
• Physical hazards relate to health, occupation, or lifestyle, while moral hazards relate to the applicant's character or intent to defraud.
• Sub-standard lives are applicants with higher-than-average risk, who are often accepted with an extra premium (loading).

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the primary function of an underwriter?
A: To assess the risk profile of the proposer and decide the terms of acceptance.
Q: Which tool provides the mathematical probability of death at different ages?
A: Mortality table.

items.title: Claims Processing
items.description:
• IRDAI guidelines mandate that an insurer must settle or reject a life insurance claim within 30 days of receiving all required documents.
• If a claim requires further investigation, it must be completed within 90 days, and the claim settled within 30 days thereafter.
• The Free-Look Period allows a policyholder to cancel the policy within 15 days of receiving the document if they disagree with the terms.
• The Standard Grace Period is 30 days for yearly/half-yearly/quarterly premium modes, and 15 days for monthly modes.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the turnaround time for an insurer to settle a claim after receiving all documents?
A: 30 days.
Q: What is the standard free-look period for a life insurance policy?
A: 15 days from the receipt of the policy document.

items.title: Documentation
items.description:
• The Proposal Form is the primary foundational document based on which the insurance contract is issued.
• The First Premium Receipt (FPR) is the conclusive proof that the insurance contract has officially commenced and risk cover has begun.
• A Renewal Premium Receipt (RPR) acts as proof of continuous payment and keeps the policy active.
• A Policy Document is the final legal evidence of the contract detailing all terms, conditions, and privileges.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which document acts as proof that the insurance contract has commenced?
A: First Premium Receipt (FPR).
Q: What is the base document for entering into a life insurance contract?
A: The Proposal Form.

items.title: Customer Service
items.description:
• According to the SERVQUAL model, Reliability (delivering what was promised) is the most critical element of service quality.
• Empathy involves giving caring, individualized attention to the customer, especially during distress like claims.
• 'Moments of Truth' occur every time a customer interacts with the insurance company, shaping their overall perception.
• Proactive customer service reduces grievances and increases policy persistency (regular renewal of policies).

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: In customer service terminology, what is a 'Moment of Truth'?
A: Any interaction where a customer forms an impression about the company.
Q: What is the most important factor in the SERVQUAL model for insurance?
A: Reliability.

items.title: Grievance Redressal Mechanism
items.description:
• The Insurance Ombudsman can pass an award up to a maximum limit of Rs. 30 Lakhs.
• A policyholder must approach the Ombudsman within 1 year of the rejection of their complaint by the insurer.
• IGMS (Integrated Grievance Management System) is the central online portal managed by IRDAI for policyholder complaints.
• No lawyers are allowed to represent either party during a hearing before the Insurance Ombudsman.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the maximum jurisdiction limit for an award by the Insurance Ombudsman?
A: Rs. 30 Lakhs.
Q: Within what time frame must a complaint be filed with the Ombudsman after the insurer rejects it?
A: 1 year.

items.title: Regulatory Aspects for Insurance Agents
items.description:
• Section 41 of the Insurance Act strictly prohibits Rebating (offering part of the commission or premium discount as an inducement).
• An insurance agent's license is valid for 3 years, after which it must be renewed.
• An agent cannot act as a director of an insurance company and must surrender the license if they wish to join an insurer's board.
• A composite agent holds licenses to sell policies for one life insurer, one general insurer, and one health insurer simultaneously.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which section of the Insurance Act prohibits rebating?
A: Section 41.
Q: What is the validity period of an insurance agent's license?
A: 3 years.

items.title: What Life Insurance Involves
items.description:
• Human Life Value (HLV), introduced by Prof. S.S. Hubner, calculates the present value of a person's future net earnings for their family.
• Mutuality is the core concept of life insurance, meaning the financial loss of one is shared among many who are exposed to the same risk.
• Life insurance deals with two major risks: dying too early (mortality) and living too long (longevity).
• Cash value in life insurance refers to the savings element that builds up over time in policies like endowment or whole life.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Who conceptualized the idea of Human Life Value (HLV)?
A: Prof. S.S. Hubner.
Q: What does Human Life Value (HLV) basically measure?
A: The economic value of a person based on their future earning capacity.

items.title: Financial Planning
items.description:
• Financial planning is the process of ensuring the right amount of money is available at the right time for specific life goals.
• Contingency planning (buying life and health insurance) must always be the first step in a sound financial plan.
• Risk profiling determines a client's risk appetite, which generally decreases as they move from the accumulation phase to the distribution (retirement) phase.
• Wealth accumulation is best achieved when investments beat inflation over the long term.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the most critical first step in personal financial planning?
A: Contingency planning and securing insurance cover.
Q: In which life stage is an individual's risk-taking capacity typically the highest?
A: Young unmarried stage (Accumulation phase).

items.title: Life Insurance Products: Traditional
items.description:
• Term Insurance is a pure risk product that pays a death benefit but offers zero maturity value or savings component.
• Endowment Insurance combines pure risk cover with a savings element, paying a lump sum upon death or maturity.
• Whole Life Insurance provides coverage up to age 99 or 100, ensuring a legacy is left for the next generation.
• Money Back Policies provide periodic survival benefits (liquidity) at regular intervals before maturity, plus full death cover.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which life insurance product offers only death cover and no maturity benefit?
A: Term Insurance.
Q: Which traditional policy is best suited for leaving a legacy for one's heirs?
A: Whole Life Insurance.

items.title: Life insurance products: Non-Traditional
items.description:
• ULIPs (Unit Linked Insurance Plans) combine investment and protection, but the investment risk is entirely borne by the policyholder.
• The value of a ULIP is determined by the NAV (Net Asset Value), representing the daily market value of one unit of the fund.
• IRDAI mandates a strict 5-year lock-in period for all ULIPs, during which no withdrawals are permitted.
• Unlike traditional plans, ULIPs are highly transparent, showing exact deductions for mortality, fund management, and administration.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: In a ULIP, who bears the investment risk?
A: The policyholder.
Q: What is the mandatory lock-in period for a Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP)?
A: 5 years.

items.title: Applications of Life Insurance
items.description:
• Section 6 of the MWP (Married Women's Property) Act ensures the policy amount is protected from the husband's creditors and forms a trust for the wife/children.
• Keyman Insurance is bought by a company on the life of a crucial employee; the company pays the premium and is the beneficiary.
• Under Keyman Insurance, the policy must strictly be a Term Insurance plan with no savings or maturity component.
• Mortgage Redemption Insurance (MRI) is a decreasing term plan designed specifically to clear an outstanding home loan if the borrower dies.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Under which Act is a life insurance policy completely protected from the policyholder's creditors and court attachments?
A: Married Women's Property (MWP) Act.
Q: Who is the beneficiary in a Keyman Insurance policy?
A: The employer / company.

items.title: Pricing and Valuation in Life Insurance
items.description:
• The formula for determining life insurance Premium is: Premium = Mortality Cost + Expenses - Interest Earned.
• Valuation is the process of comparing a life insurer's total assets against its total liabilities to determine solvency.
• Surplus is declared when Assets exceed Liabilities; a major portion of this surplus is distributed to policyholders as Bonus.
• Level Premium pricing ensures the policyholder pays the same fixed premium amount throughout the policy term, preventing unaffordable premiums in old age.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: How is the core premium calculated in life insurance?
A: Mortality Cost + Expenses - Interest.
Q: What happens when an insurer's valuation shows that Assets are greater than Liabilities?
A: A surplus is generated, which is distributed as bonuses.

items.title: Life Insurance Documentation
items.description:
• Standard Age Proofs include Passports, PAN cards, School certificates, and Birth Certificates (highly reliable).
• Non-Standard Age Proofs include horoscopes, ration cards, and village panchayat certificates (insurer may charge extra premium).
• Section 38 governs Assignment (transfer of policy ownership), while Section 39 governs Nomination (right to receive death benefit).
• Absolute Assignment completely transfers all rights of the policy to the assignee, commonly used for securing loans.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which of the following is considered a Standard Age Proof?
A: Passport.
Q: Which section of the Insurance Act deals with the Nomination of a life policy?
A: Section 39.

items.title: Life Insurance Underwriting
items.description:
• Medical Underwriting assesses the proposer's health using medical reports, while Non-Medical Underwriting relies solely on the proposal form declarations.
• Occupational hazard refers to increased risk due to a person's job (e.g., miners or circus acrobats require extra loading).
• The Principle of Proportionality dictates that the premium charged must be directly proportional to the level of risk the individual brings.
• Female underwriting may differ from male underwriting due to longevity differences and specific maternal health risks.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: A coal miner applying for life insurance represents what kind of hazard?
A: Occupational Hazard.
Q: What does Non-Medical underwriting mean?
A: Underwriting done without a medical examination, based only on the proposal form.

items.title: Life Insurance Claims
items.description:
• An 'Early Claim' is any death claim that occurs within 3 years of the policy commencement or revival date.
• Insurers investigate Early Claims thoroughly to rule out fraud, non-disclosure, or intentional concealment of material facts.
• Maturity claims require the policy document and a discharge voucher to be submitted by the policyholder before the payout.
• If an insurer delays claim payment beyond the regulatory TAT, they are liable to pay penal interest (usually bank rate + 2%).

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: A death claim arising within how many years of policy inception is classified as an Early Claim?
A: 3 years.
Q: What happens if an insurance company delays the payment of a valid claim beyond the stipulated time?
A: The insurer must pay penal interest on the claim amount.

items.title: Introduction to Health Insurance
items.description:
• Morbidity is the statistical rate of incidence of disease, illness, or sickness in a given population (the basis of health insurance pricing).
• Health insurance is based on the Principle of Indemnity, meaning it reimburses the actual hospital bill up to the sum insured, not a flat amount.
• Healthcare focuses on treatment and hospitals, whereas Health Insurance is the financing mechanism to pay for that care.
• Out-of-pocket expenses refer to the medical costs that individuals pay from their own savings because they lack insurance.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What statistical metric is used to price Health Insurance premiums?
A: Morbidity table.
Q: Health insurance contracts operate primarily on which principle?
A: Principle of Indemnity.

items.title: Health Insurance Documentation
items.description:
• TPA (Third Party Administrator) is a licensed entity appointed by the insurer to process health insurance claims and manage network hospitals.
• Portability allows a policyholder to switch their health insurance from one company to another while carrying forward their waiting period credits.
• To avail portability, the policyholder must apply to the new insurer at least 45 days before the current policy's renewal date.
• A Pre-authorization form is required to be submitted to the TPA by the hospital to approve a cashless treatment.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is the primary role of a TPA in health insurance?
A: To process claims and provide cashless services at network hospitals.
Q: How many days prior to renewal must a customer apply for porting their health insurance policy?
A: 45 days.

items.title: Health Insurance Products
items.description:
• A Family Floater policy covers the entire family under a single, shared Sum Insured, which can be utilized by any member.
• Day Care Procedures are medical treatments (like cataract or dialysis) that require less than 24 hours of hospitalization due to advanced technology.
• Domiciliary Hospitalization covers medical treatments taken at home because the patient cannot be moved or no hospital beds are available.
• Critical Illness policies are benefit policies; they pay a lump-sum amount upon the diagnosis of a specified severe disease, regardless of actual hospital bills.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Which policy provides a single shared sum insured for all members of a family?
A: Family Floater Policy.
Q: Surgeries that require less than 24 hours of hospitalization due to technological advancements are called?
A: Day Care Procedures.

items.title: Health Insurance Underwriting
items.description:
• Pre-Existing Diseases (PED) are medical conditions diagnosed or treated within 48 months before buying the health policy.
• A Co-payment clause mandates that the policyholder must pay a fixed percentage of every claim out of their own pocket.
• A Deductible is a fixed initial amount the insured must pay for medical expenses before the health insurance coverage kicks in.
• Age is the most critical underwriting factor in health insurance because morbidity (sickness rate) directly increases with age.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: What is a Pre-Existing Disease (PED) waiting period under standard IRDAI guidelines?
A: Up to 48 months.
Q: What does a 'Co-payment' clause mean in health insurance?
A: The policyholder agrees to bear a specified percentage of the claim amount.

items.title: Health Insurance Claims
items.description:
• Cashless Claims can only be availed at Network Hospitals that have a prior tie-up with the insurer or TPA.
• In a Reimbursement Claim, the patient pays the hospital bill first, collects the original documents, and files for a refund from the insurer.
• In cashless claims, the hospital interacts directly with the TPA using a pre-authorization letter, relieving the patient of financial stress.
• Claims can be rejected if the admission was solely for diagnostic or investigative purposes without active line of treatment.

🎯 HIGH-PROBABILITY EXAM Q&A:
Q: Where can a policyholder avail a Cashless claim facility?
A: At Network Hospitals tied up with the insurer/TPA.
Q: In which type of claim does the policyholder pay the bill first and then claim the money back?
A: Reimbursement Claim.
